seo.title: Homeless help in Birmingham - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Birmingham: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

page.heading: Birmingham homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance: 999 or 112 Nowhere to stay tonight, age 25+ or age 18–24 with dependent children: council 0121 303 7410, option 3, weekdays 9am–5pm Out of hours, age 18+: council 0121 303 2296 Age 16–25 with no dependent children: St Basils 0300 303 0099 Urgent but not life-threatening medical or mental-health help: NHS 111
page.notice: Beds, food, opening times and eligibility can change. Call before travelling when possible. An assessment, alert or referral does not guarantee accommodation. Never pay anyone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.
page.intro:
Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. If a service cannot help, ask for the next safe option and write down the advice.
Start here: call the council if you have nowhere tonight. If you are sleeping outside, also make a StreetLink alert so Birmingham's outreach team receives your location. For help before you lose your home, apply to the council as soon as you are at risk within 56 days.
page.footer: Is something wrong or outdated? Submit a correction. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md

entries.title: Emergency services
entries.description:
Phone: 999 or 112.
Call for: immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.
NHS guidance on calling 999

entries.title: Birmingham City Council: nowhere to stay tonight
entries.description:
Age 25+ or age 18–24 with dependent children: call 0121 303 7410, option 3, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Outside these hours, age 18+: call 0121 303 2296. Age 17 or under: call 0121 675 4806.
The council will assess your circumstances. Say if you cannot safely remain where you are, and if children, pregnancy, abuse, disability or serious health needs are involved. Temporary accommodation is not guaranteed.
Council emergency-accommodation instructions

entries.title: Council homelessness prevention: at risk within 56 days
entries.description:
Apply online: use the council form if you have somewhere tonight but may become homeless within the next 8 weeks. Submit notices, tenancy papers and income information if available, but do not wait until the final day to ask for help.
Documents: the council may ask for identity, immigration, benefits, income, bank and housing records. Call even if some documents are missing and explain why.
Apply for homelessness help

entries.title: StreetLink: alert the rough-sleeping outreach team
entries.description:
Use it for: yourself or someone sleeping outside. Give a precise public location, usual time and description. In Birmingham the alert goes to the Trident Reach outreach team.
StreetLink is not an emergency service and does not itself provide a bed. Use 999 for immediate danger and the council numbers above if you have nowhere tonight.
Make a StreetLink alert or self-referral

entries.title: Severe Weather Emergency Protocol
entries.description:
Birmingham activates extra emergency provision during severe weather warnings and when the forecast real-feel temperature is 0°C or below. Trident Reach coordinates access.
Council rough-sleeping and SWEP information
entries.how_to_access: Access: make a StreetLink self-referral or attend SIFA Fireside during its opening hours. Ask whether SWEP is active that day. A referral still requires contact and assessment.

entries.title: Domestic abuse and an unsafe home
entries.description:
All survivors at risk of homelessness: call the Cranstoun and council housing service on 0121 633 1750, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Women-only homelessness hub: 0121 272 8905, Monday–Thursday 9am–4:30pm.
Do not return to collect documents if doing so is unsafe. Refuge addresses are confidential and a place depends on assessment and availability.
Council domestic-abuse housing help

categories.title: Day centres, shelter pathways and housing support

entries.title: SIFA Fireside Support Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 766 1700. Drop-in: Monday–Friday 9am–12:45pm.
Service: homelessness assessment, housing and benefits help, breakfast, hot food, showers, laundry, clean clothing, internet, health clinics and specialist support for people with restricted benefit eligibility. It is a day centre, not a walk-in night shelter.
SIFA Fireside current services
entries.address: Address: Main entrance, Liverpool Street, Deritend, Birmingham B9 4DS

entries.title: St Basils Youth Hub: ages 16–25
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 303 0099; email: youthline@stbasils.org.uk. You can also text NEED ST BASILS to 62277. — mailto:youthline@stbasils.org.uk
Drop-in: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9am–5pm; Wednesday 1pm–5pm. For young people homeless today or at risk within 56 days. Staff assess housing, benefits, family mediation, health, education, training and employment needs.
St Basils get-help information
entries.address: Address: St Basils Centre, Heath Mill Lane, Birmingham B9 4AX

entries.title: Crisis Skylight Birmingham
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 348 7950; email: birmingham@crisis.org.uk. Open Monday–Friday 9am–5pm; if unable to call or email, drop in 9am–4pm. — mailto:birmingham@crisis.org.uk
Who: people aged 16+ who are homeless or immediately at risk. Housing, work, skills, health, wellbeing and coaching support may be offered after assessment. Crisis is not an emergency shelter and same-day appointments are not guaranteed.
Crisis Birmingham
entries.address: Address: Suite 303, Rhubarb, 25 Heath Mill Lane, Digbeth, Birmingham B9 4AE

entries.title: Birmingham City Mission Care Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 289 2894. Open: Monday–Thursday 10am–4pm.
Service: drop-in hot meals and drinks, clothes, toiletries and practical or emotional support, including help to connect with accommodation, employment, rehabilitation, benefits and health services. Birmingham City Mission is a Christian charity; ask staff if you have concerns about any activity.
City Mission Care Centre
entries.address: Address: 8–10 Washington Street, Birmingham B1 1JR

entries.title: Trident Reach housing and floating support
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 266 5800; email: customerservices@tridentgroup.org.uk. — mailto:customerservices@tridentgroup.org.uk
Trident Reach provides commissioned outreach, supported accommodation and support in Birmingham. Contact does not guarantee a vacancy; ask the council, StreetLink or SIFA which referral route applies to you.
Council list of current homelessness support

entries.title: Homeless England directory
entries.description:
Search for accommodation, day centres, outreach and specialist services by area and eligibility. Confirm each listing directly before travelling because vacancies and referral rules change.
Search Homeless England

entries.title: Closed service warning: William Booth Centre
entries.description:
The former Salvation Army accommodation at William Booth Centre closed on 30 November 2024 and is not a current shelter. Some older directories and a council advice page still show it. Use the council, StreetLink, SIFA or St Basils routes above instead.
NHS confirmation of the closure and service relocation

entries.title: SIFA Fireside
entries.description:
Breakfast and other food support are available during the weekday morning drop-in, alongside showers, clothes and casework. Arrive early and ask what is available that day.
SIFA Fireside
entries.address: Address: Liverpool Street, Deritend, Birmingham B9 4DS

entries.title: Birmingham City Mission Care Centre
entries.description:
Hot meals and drinks are available during the Monday–Thursday drop-in, 10am–4pm, with clothes, toiletries and support. Call 0121 289 2894 before a long journey.
Care Centre services
entries.address: Address: 8–10 Washington Street, Birmingham B1 1JR

entries.title: Birmingham Central Foodbank
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 236 2997. Food parcels are distributed Tuesday 9:30am–11:15am and Friday 10am–1:15pm.
The foodbank normally uses vouchers, but its published policy accepts first-time self-referrals and urgent hardship. Parcels cover about three days and toiletries, advice, phones, SIM cards or day bus passes may be available. Stock is not guaranteed.
Birmingham Central Foodbank
entries.address: Address: Birmingham City Church, Parade, Birmingham B1 3QQ; car park entrance on Helena Street B1 2AW

entries.title: Birmingham City Mission Resource Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 766 6603, extension 1; email: resources@birminghamcitymission.co.uk. Open Tuesday–Thursday 10am–4pm. — mailto:resources@birminghamcitymission.co.uk
Food parcels, toiletries, clothing, furniture and white goods are distributed through partner-agency referrals. Call first to learn who can refer you.
City Mission Resource Centre
entries.address: Address: The Clock Tower, 2 Langdon Street, Birmingham B9 4BP

entries.title: Let's Feed Brum
entries.description:
Volunteer teams provide evening food and supplies through city-centre walkabouts, plus breakfast clubs by Birmingham Cathedral on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Routes and times can change, so check the current service information rather than waiting at an old location.
Let's Feed Brum services

entries.title: As-Suffa Homeless Project
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 285 2777; email: info@as-suffa.org. — mailto:info@as-suffa.org
The Muslim charity publishes hot-meal outreach for people experiencing homelessness five times each week. Ask for the current public distribution location and time before travelling.
As-Suffa homeless support
entries.address: Address: 22 The Arch, Lionel Street, Birmingham B3 1AG

entries.title: St Chad's Sanctuary: refugees and asylum seekers
entries.description:
Phone: 07898 062765. Open Monday, Wednesday and Friday 10:30am–1:30pm, no appointment.
Food, clothing, toiletries and practical items are available for asylum seekers and refugees; Friday includes an advice service. St Chad's Sanctuary is a Catholic and Salvation Army partnership.
St Chad's Sanctuary
entries.address: Address: St Anne's Parish Centre, Alcester Street, Birmingham B12 0PH

entries.title: Riverside Community Hub
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 442 4484. Free community café and money advice Wednesday 10am–2:30pm; low-cost pantry Thursday 10am–12pm; free open lunch Sunday 1pm–3pm.
Wi-Fi, charging, toilets and warm food are listed. Confirm the week's timetable and pantry charge before travelling.
Council Riverside Hub listing
entries.address: Address: 21 Alcester Road, Moseley, Birmingham B13 8AR

entries.title: Council Food Justice Network map
entries.description:
Use the map to find foodbanks, community meals and pantries near where you are. Listings distinguish walk-in services from those requiring a voucher. Always check the provider's current opening time.
Council help-with-food map and advice

entries.title: Council emergency food voucher request
entries.description:
If you cannot use the online request, call 0121 303 1116. Published contact hours are Monday–Friday 9am–7pm and Saturday 10am–1pm. A request is assessed and does not guarantee same-day food.
Request emergency food support

entries.title: SIFA Fireside
entries.description:
Showers, laundry, clean clothing and toiletries are available alongside breakfast and casework during the weekday morning drop-in. Ask staff for a slot as early as possible.
SIFA service summary

entries.title: Birmingham City Mission Care Centre
entries.description:
Clothes and toiletries are provided when available during the Monday–Thursday drop-in. The centre also gives hot meals and practical support.
Care Centre details

entries.title: Anawim Women's Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 440 5296. Open Monday–Thursday 9am–4:30pm and Friday 9am–4pm.
Women can drop in without a referral for a hot shower, food parcels, toiletries, sanitary products, clothes and support with housing, benefits, safety, health and work.
Anawim drop-in services
entries.address: Address: 228 Mary Street, Balsall Heath, Birmingham B12 9RJ

entries.title: City Mission Resource Centre clothing
entries.description:
Free changes of clothing, toiletries and household essentials may be available through a partner-agency referral. Call 0121 766 6603, extension 1, before travelling.
Resource Centre access

entries.title: NHS urgent care
entries.description:
Emergency: 999. Urgent but not life-threatening: 111 or NHS 111 online. Tell the adviser if you have no fixed address, phone, transport or safe place to recover.
NHS 111 online

entries.title: Homeless Health Exchange
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 301 3900. Open Monday–Friday 9am–12:30pm and 1pm–5pm; closed weekends and bank holidays.
Specialist NHS primary care for people who are homeless, unstably housed, refugees or seeking asylum. Services include GP registration, physical and mental health care, wounds, vaccinations, substance-use support and blood-borne-virus testing.
NHS Homeless Primary Care Team
entries.address: Address: Attwood Green Medical Centre, 30 Bath Row, Birmingham B15 1LZ

entries.title: Register with a GP without ID or a fixed address
entries.description:
NHS rules say you do not need ID, proof of address, immigration status or an NHS number. A surgery may use a temporary address or its own address. A practice can refuse for another permitted reason, such as a closed list, but must explain a refusal in writing.
NHS GP registration guidance

entries.title: Dental Service for Homeless Adults
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 466 6880. Walk-in Thursday 1:30pm–4pm for people aged 16+ who are homeless; first come, first served until full.
NHS charges can apply unless you qualify for free treatment. The clinic may occasionally close, so call before travelling. For urgent dental pain outside the clinic, use NHS 111.
NHS homeless dental service
entries.address: Address: Third-floor dental clinic, Attwood Green Health Centre, 30 Bath Row, Birmingham B15 1LZ

entries.title: SIFA health clinics
entries.description:
SIFA's current client timetable includes a nurse, vision care, chiropody and sexual-health visits on selected weekdays. These sessions can change each month; ask reception during the morning drop-in or check the current newsletter.
SIFA client timetable

entries.title: Urgent mental-health help
entries.description:
Call 111 and choose mental-health option 2 for urgent support in Birmingham and Solihull. Call 999 if there is immediate danger to life.
Birmingham NHS urgent mental-health help

entries.title: Birmingham Mind helpline
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 262 3555, daily 9am–11pm.
Confidential listening, information and signposting for people affected by mental-health problems. It is not an emergency service or an accommodation provider.
Birmingham Mind helpline

entries.title: Samaritans
entries.description:
Phone: 116 123, free, 24 hours a day. Call if you need someone to listen, whatever you are facing. You do not need to be suicidal.
Contact Samaritans

entries.title: Change Grow Live Birmingham
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 227 5890.
Free drug and alcohol treatment, including a specialist homelessness and rough-sleeping team, prescribing, needle exchange, naloxone, blood-borne-virus tests, recovery and employment support. Call for the correct hub and current access route.
Birmingham drug and alcohol service

entries.title: Birmingham LGBT substance support
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 643 0821. LGBTQ+ people can obtain confidential substance-use support, needle exchange, sexual-health support and referrals for detoxification or rehabilitation.
Birmingham LGBT substance support
entries.address: Address: Birmingham LGBT Centre, 151 Hurst Street, Birmingham B5 6EW

categories.title: Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

entries.title: Library of Birmingham
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 242 4242. Full service Monday–Tuesday 11am–7pm and Wednesday–Saturday 11am–5pm; additional express hours operate on weekdays.
Free Wi-Fi is available throughout. Lower Terrace computers include 30-minute sessions without booking and longer sessions for library members. Ask staff about toilets, charging, membership and printing costs.
Library of Birmingham current hours
entries.address: Address: Centenary Square, Broad Street, Birmingham B1 2ND

entries.title: The Exchange Warm Welcome
entries.description: The Exchange Warm Welcome listing
entries.address: Address: 3 Centenary Square, Birmingham B1 2DR
entries.hours: Open: Monday–Friday 8am–5pm. The council lists free Wi-Fi, phone charging, workstations, refreshments and accessible toilets.

entries.title: Warm Welcome spaces across Birmingham
entries.description:
The council directory lists more than 200 community spaces. Filter for toilets, Wi-Fi, computers, charging, hot drinks or food, then contact the venue because hours and activities change.
Search Birmingham Warm Welcome spaces

entries.title: Day-centre facilities
entries.description:
SIFA publishes showers, laundry and internet; City Mission provides food and essentials; Riverside Community Hub lists Wi-Fi, charging, toilets and food. Use the earlier sections for addresses and current hours.
Council Warm Welcome information

entries.title: Plan and pay for local travel
entries.description:
Bus, tram and train fares vary. Use Transport for West Midlands to compare tickets and concessionary passes. If a journey is for housing, health or a Jobcentre appointment, ask the referring worker before travelling whether any ticket support is available.
Transport for West Midlands journey planner

entries.title: Older and disabled travel passes
entries.description:
Eligible West Midlands residents can receive free off-peak bus, train and tram travel. Proof and residence rules apply; a support worker or Disability Resource Centre can help with the application.
Travel discounts and free passes

entries.title: Workwise when starting a job
entries.description:
Eligible job starters may receive two free four-week passes and 50% off a third. Apply close to the start date and ask a Jobcentre work coach for application help if you lack internet or documents.
Workwise rules and application information

entries.title: Birmingham Airport
entries.description:
Trains run between Birmingham New Street and Birmingham International. The Air-Rail Link connects the railway station and airport terminal; it is currently operating a reduced single-train service, with a signed walking alternative. Allow extra time and check before travel.
If you are stranded at the airport, speak to airport staff or police. The airport is not an accommodation service; use the council emergency route if you have nowhere to stay.
Birmingham Airport Air-Rail update

entries.title: Universal Credit without a fixed address
entries.description:
You can claim while sleeping rough, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel if otherwise eligible. With permission, use a trusted person's, hostel's, day centre's or Jobcentre's address. Tell Jobcentre staff if you lack ID, internet, email, a bank account or a National Insurance number.
GOV.UK Universal Credit for homeless people

entries.title: Housing Benefit for supported or temporary accommodation
entries.description:
People in many hostels, refuges, supported housing or council temporary accommodation must claim Housing Benefit rather than Universal Credit housing costs. Ask the accommodation worker which claim is correct.
Council Benefits Service: 0121 464 7000.
Birmingham Housing Benefit claims

entries.title: Crisis and Resilience Fund
entries.description:
For Birmingham residents in hardship who need help with food, energy, water or essential items. Applications are assessed, funds are limited and the scheme is not a same-day emergency service.
Contact: 0121 634 7100; crf@bvsc.org. — mailto:crf@bvsc.org
Crisis and Resilience Fund 2026–27

entries.title: Discretionary Housing Payment
entries.description:
If Housing Benefit or Universal Credit housing costs do not cover your rent, ask the council about a Discretionary Housing Payment. It is means-tested, temporary and not guaranteed.
Apply for discretionary housing help

entries.title: Council cost-of-living support
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 303 1116, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm for immediate money, food, fuel or benefit problems. Ask what emergency or local support is open that day.
Birmingham living-cost support

entries.title: Benefits check and casework at SIFA, Crisis or St Basils
entries.description:
These services can help start or repair a claim, collect evidence, contact a work coach and explain housing costs. St Basils is the dedicated route for ages 16–25; SIFA and Crisis have their own assessment rules.
SIFA support services

categories.title: Work, training and travel to a new job

entries.title: Crisis Skylight work and skills support
entries.description:
Crisis coaches can support job search, training, qualifications, housing and wellbeing after an assessment. Contact the Birmingham Skylight on 0121 348 7950.
Crisis Birmingham employment support

entries.title: SIFA employability support
entries.description:
SIFA offers an employability coach, digital help and workshops alongside housing and benefits casework. The weekly timetable can change; ask during the weekday morning drop-in.
SIFA current client programme

entries.title: St Basils education, training and employment
entries.description:
Young people aged 16–25 can ask the Youth Hub for help with a safe place, benefits, qualifications, training and work. Support depends on assessment, not just attendance at one session.
St Basils Youth Hub

entries.title: Disability Resource Centre employment support
entries.description:
Phone: 03030 402040. Disabled people and people with long-term health conditions can ask about employment, training, volunteering, IT and benefits support.
Disability employment programmes

entries.title: Jobcentre Plus
entries.description:
Ask a work coach for help with a Universal Credit claim, identity checks, work-search commitments, interview costs and any travel support. Explain how homelessness affects phone, internet, clothing, sleep and transport.
Find the nearest Jobcentre

entries.title: Official job search
entries.description:
Use GOV.UK Find a Job for vacancies. SIFA, Crisis, St Basils and the library can help with email, online applications and a CV.
GOV.UK Find a Job

entries.title: Workwise travel support
entries.description:
Eligible West Midlands residents starting a job, apprenticeship or increasing work to at least 16 hours may receive two free four-week travel passes and a third at half price. Apply online from 10 working days before to 10 working days after starting and provide job evidence.
A Jobcentre work coach can help if you lack a computer. The award is not automatic and cannot be combined with some other travel schemes.
Transport for West Midlands Workwise rules

categories.title: Housing law, debt and legal advice

entries.title: Shelter Birmingham
entries.description:
Legal-aid appointments: 0344 515 1875, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Shelter advises on homelessness, council decisions, eviction, rent and disrepair. An appointment and legal-aid eligibility check are required.
Emergency housing helpline: 0808 800 4444.
Shelter Birmingham
entries.address: Address: Unit 38, The Priory, Queensway, Birmingham B4 7LA

entries.title: Central England Law Centre housing team
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 227 6540; email: bhamenquiries@centralenglandlc.org.uk. — mailto:bhamenquiries@centralenglandlc.org.uk
Housing and homelessness advice, legal-aid casework and court representation may be available. Capacity and eligibility limits apply; call before attending.
Birmingham housing legal help

entries.title: Citizens Advice Birmingham debt line
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 330 2130, Monday–Friday 9am–3pm; email: debthelp@bcabs.cabnet.org.uk. — mailto:debthelp@bcabs.cabnet.org.uk
Free advice on rent, council tax, energy and other debt. The service states that there is no city-centre walk-in, so call or email first.
Citizens Advice Birmingham debt help

entries.title: Birmingham Settlement money advice
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 250 0777; email: money.advice@bsettlement.org.uk. Ask about benefits, debt, budgeting and the nearest available appointment. — mailto:money.advice@bsettlement.org.uk
Council-listed benefits and money advice

entries.title: Civil Legal Advice
entries.description:
Phone: 0345 345 4345. Free and confidential legal-aid advice may be available for eligible housing, domestic-abuse, debt and discrimination matters. Ask for a callback if you cannot afford the call.
Civil Legal Advice

entries.title: Council assessment documents
entries.description:
Bring what you safely have: photo ID, immigration papers, children's birth certificates, benefit or income evidence, bank statements, tenancy agreement and any notice requiring you to leave. Do not delay an urgent call because a document is missing.
Council list of documents

entries.title: National Insurance number
entries.description:
You may be able to find the number on a payslip, P60, tax account or HMRC app. You can start a Universal Credit claim without knowing it. Apply for a number if you have the right to work in the UK and do not already have one.
Apply for a National Insurance number

entries.title: Right-to-work evidence
entries.description:
If you hold digital immigration status, GOV.UK can create a share code for an employer. Get regulated immigration advice if your status or work conditions are unclear.
Prove your right to work

entries.title: Passport advice if homeless or missing documents
entries.description:
Contact the Passport Adviceline before paying for an application. Ask a SIFA, Crisis, St Basils or migrant-support caseworker to help explain your circumstances and arrange a safe delivery address. Never use a service's address without written permission.
HM Passport Office Adviceline

entries.title: Phone, SIM card and online access
entries.description:
Birmingham Central Foodbank may have phones or SIM cards; SIFA provides internet and digital support; the Library of Birmingham has free Wi-Fi and computers. Availability and eligibility vary.
Foodbank additional support

entries.title: Mail and storage
entries.description:
Ask your named worker whether the council, hostel, SIFA, Crisis, St Basils or Jobcentre can authorise a care-of address. Ask where identity documents can be stored safely. No verified open-access luggage-storage service was found in Birmingham.
Do not: send post or leave belongings at any service without permission. Ask about collection deadlines and what happens if you move.
Official care-of address options for Universal Credit

entries.title: Refugee and Migrant Centre Birmingham
entries.description:
General phone: 0800 0663 444. Drop-in Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9am–1pm; appointments 2pm–5pm. Emergency cases are prioritised, but appointments are limited.
Advice and casework for refugees, asylum seekers and migrants. The office has reported a temporary lift outage; attend and tell staff if stairs are not accessible so they can make arrangements.
RMC centres and current hours
entries.address: Address: Second Floor, Chamberlain Building, 36 Frederick Street, Birmingham B1 3HN

entries.title: St Chad's Sanctuary
entries.description:
Refugees and asylum seekers can receive food, clothing, toiletries, information and Friday advice without an appointment, Monday, Wednesday and Friday 10:30am–1:30pm.
St Chad's Sanctuary
entries.address: Address: St Anne's Parish Centre, Alcester Street, Birmingham B12 0PH

entries.title: Migrant Help asylum helpline
entries.description:
Phone: 0808 8010 503, free. Published hours are Monday–Friday 8am–8pm, with 24-hour emergency assistance.
For people who have claimed or intend to claim asylum: asylum-support accommodation, destitution, reporting housing problems and finding legal representation. Migrant Help does not itself provide legal representation.
GOV.UK asylum helplines

entries.title: Modern Slavery and Exploitation Helpline
entries.description:
Phone: 08000 121 700. Current temporary hours are 12 noon–5pm daily. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Confidential information and guidance if someone is controlled, threatened, forced to work, sexually exploited or has documents or pay withheld. You do not have to give your name.
Modern Slavery Helpline

entries.title: Birmingham and Solihull Women's Aid
entries.description:
Helpline: 0808 800 0028, Monday–Friday 9:30am–5pm.
Confidential domestic-abuse support, safety planning and refuge referrals for women and children. A referral does not guarantee a refuge place. In immediate danger call 999.
Birmingham and Solihull Women's Aid

entries.title: Theresa Stewart Women's Centre
entries.description:
Women's Aid drop-in: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 10am–4pm; Wednesday 1pm–4pm. Ask for safety, housing, benefit and domestic-abuse support.
Women's Aid services and contact
entries.address: Address: 36 Bristol Street, Birmingham B5 7AA

entries.title: WAITS: women affected by domestic abuse
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 440 1443; email: support@waitsaction.org. — mailto:support@waitsaction.org
WAITS supports women and operates confidential emergency accommodation for single women aged 20+ affected by domestic abuse. Self-referrals and professional referrals are accepted; a place depends on assessment and vacancies.
WAITS access information

entries.title: Anawim Women's Centre
entries.description:
Women can drop in without a referral for food, toiletries, a shower and help with housing, benefits, violence, mental health, criminal justice and employment. Call 0121 440 5296.
Anawim women's drop-in
entries.address: Address: 228 Mary Street, Balsall Heath, Birmingham B12 9RJ

entries.title: St Basils: ages 16–25
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 303 0099. The Youth Hub is Birmingham's dedicated homelessness route for young people without dependent children. Under 18 and out of hours, call the council Emergency Duty Team on 0121 675 4806.
St Basils Youth Hub

entries.title: Birmingham LGBT Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 643 0821; email: hello@blgbt.org. Open Monday–Wednesday 10am–6pm, Thursday–Friday 10am–9pm and Saturday 10:30am–6pm. — mailto:hello@blgbt.org
Specialist counselling, sexual health, substance-use and domestic-abuse support. It is not a shelter; ask for a safe referral if homelessness or violence is involved.
Birmingham LGBT current centre and hours
entries.address: Address: 151 Hurst Street, Birmingham B5 6EW

entries.title: Op FORTITUDE: veterans
entries.description:
Phone: 0800 952 0774. Veterans who are homeless or at risk can self-refer to the national government-backed housing pathway. Advice and accommodation searches depend on assessment and availability.
GOV.UK Op FORTITUDE

entries.title: Age UK Birmingham: age 50+
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 437 0479; email: info@ageukbirmingham.org.uk. — mailto:info@ageukbirmingham.org.uk
Information, advice and helpline support for people aged 50+, families and carers. Say immediately if you are homeless, unsafe or being discharged from hospital without suitable accommodation.
Council Age UK Birmingham listing

entries.title: Disability Resource Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 03030 402040; email: drc@disability.co.uk. Advice includes benefits, debt, grants, housing, equipment, transport and employment. — mailto:drc@disability.co.uk
Call before travelling. The centre is open to visitors Monday–Thursday 8:45am–5pm; staff work remotely or in the community on Friday.
Disability information and advice
entries.address: Address: Unit 18, Ace Business Park, Mackadown Lane, Kitts Green, Birmingham B33 0LD

entries.title: Adult social care and safeguarding
entries.description:
Phone: 0121 303 1234. Contact the council if an adult cannot keep themselves safe because of disability, illness, age, abuse or neglect. Emergency housing still requires the homelessness routes above.
Deaf or hard-of-hearing callers can use SignLive or dial 18001 before the council number.
Council contact and accessibility options

entries.title: Child protection and families
entries.description:
Concern about a child: 0121 303 1888. Out of hours: 0121 675 4806. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Tell the housing team if children are with you and you have nowhere safe tonight. Do not leave a child sleeping outside while waiting for an online reply.
Birmingham safeguarding numbers

entries.title: StreetVet Birmingham
entries.description:
StreetVet provides free veterinary outreach for pets belonging to people experiencing homelessness, usually through partner services and at least two Birmingham outreach clinics each month. Locations and dates change; use the official help form or ask SIFA or an outreach worker.
StreetVet is not a general emergency vet. In an animal emergency, contact the last vet, PDSA, RSPCA or any veterinary practice for immediate advice.
StreetVet Birmingham

entries.title: Dogs Trust Together Through Homelessness
entries.description:
The scheme can help participating homelessness services with free veterinary treatment and maintains a directory of dog-friendly accommodation. Ask your council, SIFA, Crisis or hostel worker to check the current referral route.
Dogs Trust homelessness support

entries.title: Tell every service about your pet
entries.description:
Many placements cannot accept animals; some can. Tell the council, StreetLink and any referrer the species, size, vaccination status and whether temporary foster care is possible. Do not abandon an animal or arrive at an unknown hostel expecting it to be admitted.
